designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch the state you will keep per rate-limited entity and how you will decide whether a request is allowed right now. Name the data structure backing the sliding window.

parts.title: Single-key sliding window

hints.text: What is the minimum state you need to know whether the last window_seconds contained fewer than capacity requests?
A count-and-reset-at-fixed-boundaries counter is simple but wrong right at the boundary. Consider keeping every recent request's timestamp instead.
Keep a deque of timestamps. On each call, drop everything at or before now - window_seconds from the front, then compare the remaining length to capacity.

probes: What happens right at the boundary between one window and the next?
What is the time complexity of allow() as old requests age out?

parts.title: Independent per-key limits

hints.text: Your part-1 state was for one caller. What has to change so each key gets its own, independent budget?
A map from key to whatever state part 1 kept works — the interesting question is what happens for a key you have never seen before.
Keep unordered_map<string, deque<double>>, created lazily on first use. Everything else from part 1 stays the same, just scoped to one bucket per key.

probes: What did keying by identity cost you that a single global limiter did not have?
Does a key that has never sent a request take up any memory before its first call?

parts.title: Per-key overrides and bounded memory

hints.text: You now need two more things tracked per key: an optional custom capacity, and when that key was last used.
Track last-used time per key. When adding a brand-new key would exceed max_keys, evict whichever existing key has the oldest last-used time — and make sure eviction removes ALL of that key's state.
Keep a small struct per key: {bucket, capacity_override, last_used}. On allow(), touch last_used and use capacity_override if set.

probes: If you evict a key, what happens to a limit you had configured for it?
How would a caller know how long to wait before retrying, without just calling allow() in a loop?

criteria: sliding window is accurate at the window boundary
per-key state introduced deliberately, not bolted on
eviction keeps override state and usage state consistent
deque used for O(1) eviction from the front
boundary and eviction edge cases considered before being told
stated the tradeoff of adding per-key state and bounded memory
